title: Give release.yml's registry verification a longer window with backoff, distinguishing 'not yet visible' from 'wrong content'
description: Counterpart of quest-cli's QCLI-247. The registry-propagation lag on @opum-ai/lore-linux-arm64 specifically has now recurred on three consecutive releases and is strictly worsening, not random jitter: 0.4.5 resolved in ~15s, 0.4.6 in ~35s, 0.5.0 took ~25 minutes (resolved 2026-09-08T14:49:18Z) before registry.npmjs.org's versions map showed the just-published 0.5.0 -- confirmed via response headers directly (cf-cache-status/age) that this was a genuine origin-side gap, not a stale CDN cache. npm's own publish confirmation (the job log's '+ @opum-ai/lore-linux-arm64@0.5.0' line) was correct every time; only the registry read API lagged. This release, the lag ran long enough that opum-cli-e2e independently flagged it as a possible install-breaking defect before it resolved on its own -- a false alarm that cost real investigation time on both sides. See docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md's 0.5.0 entry for the full timeline and evidence.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release.yml's post-publish registry verification step polls with a longer window and backoff (not a fixed short timeout), sized against the observed 3-release lag history (up to ~25+ minutes) rather than the historical ~35s worst case

The verification step's failure output distinguishes a version genuinely missing from the registry ("not yet visible", retry/backoff territory) from a version present but reporting different content/metadata ("wrong content", a real defect worth escalating immediately) -- these must never be reported identically
The three-release lag history (0.4.5 ~15s, 0.4.6 ~35s, 0.5.0 ~25min) is recorded as the evidence justifying the new window, so a future session does not re-diagnose this from scratch
